In the eclipse prayer the Prophet reached for a bunch of Paradise's fruit, and once he saw Paradise and Hell displayed on the mosque's qibla wall.
After death each person is shown his place in Paradise or Hell morning and evening; the Prophet saw the poor most numerous in Paradise and women most numerous in Hell.
Hell keeps asking for more until Allah puts His Foot over it; Paradise and Hell argue over who enters them, and Allah says each will have its fill.
The people of Paradise are the weak and humble whose oaths Allah fulfils, and the people of Hell are the violent, arrogant and stubborn.
The Prophet saw that most in Paradise were the poor and most in the Fire were women, explaining after the eclipse prayer that they were ungrateful to their husbands.
The people of Paradise are the obscure and humble, whose oaths by Allah He fulfils, and the people of the Fire are the cruel, violent, proud and conceited.
After leading the prayer, the Prophet said Paradise and Hell had been shown to him towards the mosque wall, the best and worst things he had ever seen.
The Fire is surrounded by desires and Paradise by disliked things, and each is nearer to a person than the strap of his shoe.
Adam will be told to bring out the people of the Fire, nine hundred ninety-nine of every thousand, yet the Prophet hopes his followers will be half of Paradise's people.
Once all enter Paradise or the Fire, death will be slaughtered between them and eternity announced; the Prophet saw most in Paradise were poor and most in the Fire women.
Each sees his place in the other abode; the sincere monotheist wins the Prophet's intercession; the last man out of the Fire gets ten worlds; Abbas asks about Abu Talib.
The people of Paradise are every poor, humble person whose oath Allah fulfils, and the people of the Fire every violent, cruel, arrogant person.
